observations:
All conceptual domains in Torah #54 are well-represented by the six proposed packages and can be accommodated within them. No independent bechina domain of 3+ concepts was found that is structurally separate from the existing six packages.

The ten gap concepts identified in torah_54_additions.json each attach naturally to existing packages:
  - שֵׁם מָלֵא, נִדְמוּ, אֶחָד (אַהֲבָה נְפוּלָה) → extend Packages 1 and 2
  - עֵץ הַחַיִּים → extends Package 4 (contentment/Tzaddik)
  - גָּדַלְתָּ מְאֹד, מְאֹד, חַיֵּי שָׁעָה, אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ → extend Package 5 (daily mitzvot)
  - מִתַּחְתַּי, חָטְמִי → extend Package 6 (kohen/love)

None of these form an independent thematic family of 3+ bechina-connected concepts that would require a new package.

The Torah's argument follows a clear six-stage structure that maps cleanly onto the six packages:
  Stage 1 — Aspire to memory of the World to Come [Package 1: good]
  Stage 2 — Guard against the imagination that kills memory [Package 2: evil]
  Stage 3 — The evil eye / death of the heart is the mechanism of forgetting [Package 3: evil]
  Stage 4 — Torah/contentment/Tzaddik/commerce are the positive framework [Package 4: good]
  Stage 5 — The daily mitzvot (sleep, tzitzit, tefillin, joy, prayer) provide access for everyone [Package 5: good]
  Stage 6 — The kohen/love/Mashiach quality defeats the evil eye [Package 6: good]

The good/evil mirror structure is clearly present:
  Package 1 (Memory/World to Come) ↔ Package 2 (Evil Imagination) — the imagination is precisely what kills memory
  Package 3 (Evil Eye/Death of Heart) ↔ Package 6 (Kohen/Love/Good Eye) — the evil eye is the mirror of the good eye; the dead heart mirrors the dveikut-heart
  Package 4 (Torah/Contentment/Tzaddik) does not have a direct evil mirror in this Torah — the focus is on the positive teaching
  Package 5 (Daily Mitzvot) does not have an evil mirror — these are the tools, not contested domains

Two potential candidate new packages were considered and rejected:

Candidate A: 'דַּעַת וְאַהֲבָה' (Da'at and Love) — the teaching in section 5 extensively discusses how loss of da'at (knowledge) leads to falling from sacred love (אַהֲבוֹת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה = Package 6/kohen) to animal love. The conceptual triad of da'at/love/kohen appears frequently with bechina language. However, all these bechina nodes (כֹּהֵן = אַהֲבָה = אַבְרָהָם אוֹהֲבִי) are already in Package 6, and דַּעַת itself does not appear as a bechina node in the dataset for reference 54 (it appears only in eitza edges — loss of da'at CAUSES imagination to dominate; da'at is not equated to something else via bechina language in this Torah). Therefore no new package is warranted.

Candidate B: 'נִגּוּן וְרוּחַ נְבוּאָה' (Song and Prophetic Spirit) — sections 7-8 of the Torah develop an extended discussion of the musician and gathering spirits. However, the nodes מְנַגֵּן בַּיָּד, שִׂמְחָה, יָד are in Package 5 (joy/music as daily instrument), and the destination of the music (רוּחַ נְבוּאָה, זִכָּרוֹן) is in Package 1. The musical domain is an eitza bridge between Packages 1 and 5 rather than a self-contained bechina cluster needing its own package. The three nodes {שִׂמְחָה, מְנַגֵּן בַּיָּד, יָד} form a sub-component within Package 5, not an independent domain.
